Paper · 28 May 2025

Triplet substrates under pH and freeze-thaw cycles enable exponential RNA replication by a ribozyme

Attwater, Augustin, Curran, Kwok, Ohlendorf, Gianni, Holliger · Nature Chemistry 17:1129-1137

In a sentence

An RNA enzyme replicated both strands of short double-stranded RNAs exponentially, including a piece of itself.

In plain words

Copied RNA strands stick to their templates so tightly that copying stalls. This team found that the three-letter RNA pieces used as building blocks also hold the separated strands apart. Combined with cycles of freezing, thawing and acidity changes, an RNA polymerase ribozyme could replicate both strands of short RNAs over and over, including a fragment of the ribozyme itself. Started from random RNA, the system produced either a few winning replicators or slowly drifting mixtures.

Technical detail

Triplets bind and kinetically trap dissociated strands while serving as substrates, overcoming the strand-separation problem. With coupled pH and freeze-thaw cycles: exponential replication of (+) and (-) strands of dsRNAs, including a ribozyme fragment. Open-ended replication of random pools yielded defined replicators or diverse pools from partial ribozyme self-replication, drifting toward hypothesised primordial codons. Substrates are supplied by the experimenter.

What we take from it

Planned test

Corrects our site, which said 'no exponential growth yet' for RNA world. Ladder level L3 still needs the whole replicator copied from a setting's own feedstocks.

Source checked against its DOI. Read the original.
